{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Co-Development Agreement (Execution Version)

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Co-Development Agreement (we represent PB, the Customer)  
**Status:** 18 rules reviewed — 5 deviations, 12 compliant, 1 requires manual review

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Execution Version against the playbook. The commercial architecture is a development-financing structure in which SFJ funds the clinical program against contingent Approval Payments, and much of the agreement is favourable to us: we own the Trial Inventions, Trial Data Package and Research Results outright, SFJ (not PB) carries the only exclusivity and non-compete covenants, SFJ has no audit right against us, there is no MFN, no minimum purchase commitment and no auto-renewal, and the insurance and post-termination transition provisions run substantially in our favour.

The issues cluster in two places: **termination economics** and **liability allocation**. Three findings are, on their face, walk-away territory under the playbook — SFJ's sole-discretion right to terminate on our change of control (with a 150% payment), the punitive liquidated sums payable by us on termination (300% of Development Costs, plus 25% per annum interest on a non-breach trigger), and SFJ's discretionary terminations with no notice floor. Separately, Section 15.11 contains no aggregate monetary cap at all, leaving each Party's direct liability unlimited, and the only third-party IP infringement indemnity runs one way against us.

One rule — ownership of deliverables and Customer Data (IP) — could not be completed by the automated review and requires manual sign-off before we send comments. We should not represent our IP position as cleared until that is done.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Needs review** (verification failed) | — |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 15.3.2 If to SFJ: |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | TERM AND TERMINATION |
| High | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | TERM AND TERMINATION |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | TERM AND TERMINATION |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 3.9 IDMC |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND PERSONALLY IDENTIFIABLE INFORMATION |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 3.9 IDMC |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | RECORDS |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (at fallback) | § 15.3.2 If to SFJ: |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | SECURITY INTEREST |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | DEVELOPMENT COSTS |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant (at fallback) | § 15.3.2 If to SFJ: |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | TERM AND TERMINATION |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | TERM AND TERMINATION |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE |

---

## Deviations and proposed redlines

**1. No liability cap (Critical — § 15.3.2 If to SFJ:).** Section 15.11 is the only limitation-of-liability provision; Article 12 addresses indemnities and insurance limits only, and Section 13.6 is a warranty disclaimer. Section 15.11 gives a mutual waiver of indirect and consequential damages and confirms PB's Article 6 / 14.2 payment obligations are not limited, but there is no aggregate monetary cap, so each Party's direct liability is unlimited. That fails our fallback (mutual cap of at least 12 months' fees with carve-outs). *Proposal:* add a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' Article 6 payments and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims (indemnification, confidentiality/data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) and preserved uncapped treatment of each Party's payment/funding obligations. The existing consequential-damages exclusion and payment carve-out remain intact.

**2. Change-of-control termination right (High — TERM AND TERMINATION).** Section 15.6 itself is acceptable and at or near our preferred position: mutual, with consent-free assignment to an Affiliate or a successor by merger, stock sale or sale of substantially all assets, subject to a guarantee/continuing-liability mechanic (the absence of a "not unreasonably withheld" qualifier on other assignments is noted only). The problem is Article 14: Section 14.2.6 gives SFJ a sole-discretion right to terminate the entire Agreement following a Change of Control of PB, triggering payment of 150% of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ. A counterparty termination and effective re-pricing right on our change of control is walk-away territory and undercuts the M&A freedom in Section 15.6. *Proposal:* delete SFJ's change-of-control termination right and the associated 150% payment, retaining PB's notice obligation and the Section 15.6 assumption/guarantee protection, and delete the consequential paragraph that operates only on such a termination. PB's own Change of Control Buy-Out Option in Section 6.7.2 is in our favour and is not flagged.

**3. One-way IP indemnity (High — INDEMNIFICATION AND INSURANCE).** Article 12 contains a mutual indemnity with a proper procedure (notice, control of defence, participation, cooperation), and SFJ's limb in 12.1.1 covers its gross negligence/wilful misconduct, material breach and Protocol breaches. However, the only third-party IP infringement indemnity runs one way: under 12.1.2(f) PB indemnifies SFJ for infringement "by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder", so we carry SFJ's own infringement risk while receiving no IP indemnity from SFJ. That fails the fallback. *Proposal:* add an SFJ IP limb covering infringement arising from SFJ's (and its Affiliates'/Permitted Third Parties') performance, and delete "either Party" from 12.1.2(f) so our indemnity is confined to the Product and our own performance. The balance of PB's operating-party indemnity is left as the existing bargain.

**4. Punitive termination payments (High — TERM AND TERMINATION).** Section 14.4.2 confirms the fixed sums payable by PB under Section 14.2 are "in lieu of any claim for damages that SFJ may have" — liquidated amounts payable by us. Two fail on material terms: (i) Section 14.2.1 requires PB to pay 300% of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ (roughly $360M against the $120M funding benchmark in Section 6.2) within days of a breach termination, while we remain liable for Approval Payments; and (ii) Section 14.2.10 adds 25% per annum interest to a termination triggered not by breach but by PB's good-faith exercise of its own decision-making authority under Section 5.2.4. Punitive amounts triggered by non-material or non-breach events are walk-away territory. Given the financing structure, deleting the payment outright would be disproportionate. *Proposal:* return of the Development Costs SFJ actually funded — the same measure SFJ already accepted in Section 14.2.9 — with the 3x multiple and 25% uplift removed. We have not separately reopened the 150%/300% figures in Sections 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.6, 14.2.7 or 14.2.8.1; these should be conformed if the principle is accepted. SFJ's contingent Approval Payments and the optional Buy-Out Payments under Section 6.7 are the priced commercial bargain and are not flagged.

**5. Termination for convenience — both limbs (High — TERM AND TERMINATION).** Our only at-will right, Section 14.2.2, is double-gated: unavailable until SFJ has paid or incurred $60 million of Development Costs and unavailable at all once the first Regulatory Approval is received, priced at 300% of Development Costs paid or incurred. Over a multi-year term that is effectively no usable convenience right, and the exit charge far exceeds the fallback. On SFJ's side, Sections 14.2.6 (Change of Control) and 14.2.10 (JSC disagreement) each permit SFJ "in its sole discretion" to terminate "in its entirety at any time" with no stated notice period, and 14.2.3 permits immediate termination on a Material Adverse Event — counterparty walk-away on fewer than 90 days' notice. *Proposal (fallback, not preferred, given the funding structure):* make PB's at-will right exercisable at any time on 90 days' notice with the $60M and pre-approval gates removed, reduce the exit payment to the 150% multiple SFJ already accepts in Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.8.1, and impose a 90-day notice floor on SFJ's discretionary terminations. Section 6.7 buy-out pricing is a payments term and is not double-flagged.

---

## Compliant — no redline (noted for the file)

- **Exclusivity / Non-compete:** the only exclusivity and field-of-use covenants (Section 3.19, "Exclusive Period", "Competing Product", "Brilinta Competing Product") bind SFJ, not us. Nothing obliges PB to source from SFJ or restricts the products we may build or buy. Section 7.5.5's Licensing Transaction consent gate is a financing-style covenant over IP and royalty streams, not exclusive dealing.
- **Licence scope:** we hold the relevant IP by ownership, not licence (11.1.1.1, 11.1.1.3(a)–(b), 11.1.1.4), with a worldwide, royalty-free, fully-paid, freely-assignable multi-tier sublicensable licence as the fallback where assignment cannot be obtained. Noted only: contractor licences are on a commercially reasonable efforts basis with a background/improvement carve-out in 11.1.1.3(c), and the AZ License prevails over conflicting terms.
- **Audit:** SFJ has no audit or inspection right against us — better than our preferred position, so we will not propose inserting one. If SFJ later seeks a records audit, condition it on once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, an independent auditor under confidentiality, SFJ's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no system access.
- **Governing law and venue:** Section 15.9 selects Delaware law, which sits at our fallback rather than preferred New York law; ICDR arbitration is seated in New York under the FAA, with IP validity disputes reserved to U.S. federal court and injunctive relief available in any competent court. No foreign law, venue or seat. Non-material sub-elements noted only.
- **Non-solicitation:** Section 15.16 sits at the fallback — mutual, limited to personnel involved in development activities, solicitation-only (no no-hire), with a general-advertising carve-out. The tail duration is redacted ([***]) and runs from expiry of the Term; see next steps.
- **MFN / minimum commitments / renewal / transition / warranty / insurance:** each meets the preferred position or fallback as recorded in the findings. Transition (Section 14.3, 11.1.1.4, 3.11.1, 10.3) and insurance (Section 12.3) run materially in our favour, with redacted periods and limits to be confirmed.

---

## Walk-away items

1. **SFJ's termination right on a Change of Control of PB** (Section 14.2.6), together with the 150% Development Cost payment — an express walk-away under the assignment rule.
2. **Punitive liquidated sums payable by us:** the 300% multiple in Section 14.2.1 and the 25% per annum interest attached to a non-breach trigger in Section 14.2.10 (PB's good-faith exercise of Section 5.2.4 authority).
3. **SFJ's sole-discretion terminations with no notice floor** (Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.10) and immediate termination on a Material Adverse Event (Section 14.2.3) — counterparty walk-away on fewer than 90 days' notice.
4. **Contingent:** if the redacted non-solicit tail in Section 15.16 exceeds 24 months, that is a separate walk-away item to raise on the unredacted copy.

---

## Next steps

1. **Complete the IP review.** The ownership-of-deliverables and Customer Data rule failed automated verification and requires manual review. We should not sign off on the IP position or send comments on Article 11 until this is closed, notwithstanding the favourable ownership findings recorded under the licence rule.
2. **Issue the five redlines** in the order above, leading on the termination package (items 2–5 in the deviations list), which are commercially linked and should be negotiated as one trade.
3. **Obtain the unredacted copy** and confirm: the non-solicit tail in Section 15.16 (must not exceed 24 months); the delivery period in Section 14.3.3 (at least 30 days) and the trial-continuation period in Section 14.3.4 (at least 90 days); and the insurance limits in Section 12.3.
4. **Confirm the conforming changes** to the 150%/300% figures in Sections 14.2.2, 14.2.5.2, 14.2.6, 14.2.7 and 14.2.8.1 if SFJ accepts the actual-cost-recovery principle.
5. **Escalate to the business** the trade-off on the liability cap: we are proposing a mutual cap where none exists, which also caps SFJ's exposure to us. Confirm the business is content before we send.
"}
